translated_text:
By this I mean that all events have come to pass
Through His power and His will alone.

Our Sovereign deserves praise for all that He has willed—
Praise surpassing every commendation.

His mercy has spread throughout creation,
With manifestations of wisdom beyond the wisest minds:

Matters that bewilder the mind when it beholds
Their sublime wisdom and every wondrous thing.

We believe that Allah is mighty in His power,
His creation, and His unfailing execution of what He wills.

We affirm all this of our God,
And affirm every wisdom it contains.

This is a subject whose deniers have long failed to grasp,
Turning back in bewilderment.

To establish its truth by explaining its depths
And precisely distinguishing the truth concerning this reality

Is the highest aim of those who approach its ocean;
Yet this is difficult within the verse of this poem,

For it requires an exposition that accurately explains
The noble attributes of our Lord and God,

His most beautiful names, the rulings of His religion,
And His actions throughout this creation.

This, praise be to Allah, has become abundantly clear;
His inspiring creation with this understanding is the finest blessing.

This has been spoken of, and the written text of His Book
Offers an exposition that heals ailing souls.

Your asking, “Why did He will this?”
Is like someone asking, “Why did He exist from eternity?”

Reason rejects the very basis of that question,
And every revealed law has forbidden it.

The universe contains countless particular features, showing
Anyone with a measure of reason that they proceed from will.

وَإِنَّ ملاحيد الْفَلَاسِفَةِ الْأُولَى … يَقُولُونَ بِالْفِعْلِ الْقَدِيمِ لِعِلَّةِ
بَغَوْا عِلَّةً لِلْكَوْنِ بَعْدَ انْعِدَامِهِ … فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا ذَاكُمْ فَضَلُّوا بِضَلَّةِ
وَإِنَّ مبادي الشَّرِّ فِي كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ … ذَوِي مِلَّةٍ مَيْمُونَةٍ نَبَوِيَّةِ
بخوضهمو فِي ذَاكُمْ صَارَ شِرْكُهُمْ … وَجَاءَ دُرُوسُ الْبَيِّنَاتِ بِفَتْرَةِ
وَيَكْفِيكَ نَقْضًا أَنَّ مَا قَدْ سَأَلْتَهُ … مِنْ الْعُذْرِ مَرْدُودٌ لَدَى كُلِّ فِطْرَةِ
فَأَنْتَ تَعِيبُ الطَّاعِنِينَ جَمِيعَهُمْ … عَلَيْكَ وَتَرْمِيهِمْ بِكُلِّ مَذَمَّةِ
وَتَنْحَلُ مَنْ وَالَاكَ صَفْوَ مَوَدَّةٍ … وَتُبْغِضُ مَنْ ناواك مِنْ كُلِّ فِرْقَةِ
وَحَالُهُمْ فِي كُلِّ قَوْلٍ وَفِعْلَةٍ … كَحَالِكَ يَا هَذَا بِأَرْجَحِ حُجَّةِ
وَهَبْكَ كَفَفْتَ اللَّوْمَ عَنْ كُلِّ كَافِرٍ … وَكُلِّ غَوِيٍّ خَارِجٍ عَنْ مَحَبَّةِ
فَيَلْزَمُكَ الْإِعْرَاضُ عَنْ كُلِّ ظَالِمٍ … عَلَى النَّاسِ فِي نَفْسٍ وَمَالٍ وَحُرْمَةِ
translated_text:
And tracing its origin through one thing after another,
Or appealing to mere possibility, is a bewildered conjecture.

There is no doubt that every effect depends
On a preceding cause that necessitates it.

The real issue concerns the causes—the causes of all you see—
And their proceeding from the Sovereign Judge through His will alone.

Your asking, “Why did God will this?”
Is what plunged human minds into the depths of a pit.

For the Magians, who affirm a creator of benefit
And a lord who brings harm into being—

Their asking about the reason behind this mystery
Entangled their forebears in the delusion of dualism.

And those heretical philosophers who maintain
That action is eternal, owing to a cause,

Sought a cause for the universe’s existence after nonexistence;
Finding none, they went grievously astray.

In every community professing a blessed, prophetic faith,
Evil began through their delving into this:

From it arose their associating partners with Allah,
And the clear proofs faded during a lapse of prophetic guidance.

It is sufficient to refute you that the excuse you seek
Is rejected by every human being’s innate nature.

You blame all those who attack you,
And heap every reproach upon them.

You bestow sincere affection upon your allies,
And hate those who oppose you, whatever their faction.

Yet in every word and deed, their position is like yours,
As the weightiest proof establishes.

Suppose you withheld blame from every disbeliever
And every misguided person who is no object of love:

You would then have to turn away from every oppressor
Who violates people’s persons, property, or honour.

original_text:
وَلَا تَغْضَبَنْ يَوْمًا عَلَى سَافِكٍ دَمًا … وَلَا سَارِقٍ مَالًا لِصَاحِبِ فَاقَةِ
وَلَا شَاتِمٍ عِرْضًا مَصُونًا وَإِنْ عَلَا … وَلَا نَاكِحٍ فَرْجًا عَلَى وَجْهِ غِيَّةِ
وَلَا قَاطِعٍ لِلنَّاسِ نَهْجَ سَبِيلِهِمْ … وَلَا مُفْسِدٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ فِي كُلِّ وجهة
وَلَا شَاهِدٍ بِالزُّورِ إفْكًا وَفِرْيَةً … وَلَا قَاذِفٍ لِلْمُحْصَنَاتِ بِزَنْيَةِ
وَلَا مُهْلِكٍ لِلْحَرْثِ وَالنَّسْلِ عَامِدًا … وَلَا حَاكِمٍ لِلْعَالَمِينَ بِرِشْوَةِ
وَكُفَّ لِسَانَ اللَّوْمِ عَنْ كُلِّ مُفْسِدٍ … وَلَا تَأْخُذَنْ ذَا جرمة بِعُقُوبَةِ
وَسَهِّلْ سَبِيلَ الْكَاذِبِينَ تَعَمُّدًا … عَلَى رَبِّهِمْ مِنْ كُلِّ جَاءٍ بِفِرْيَةِ
وَإِنْ قَصَدُوا إضْلَالَ مَنْ يَسْتَجِيبُهُمْ … بِرَوْمِ فَسَادِ النَّوْعِ ثُمَّ الرِّيَاسَةِ
وَجَادِلْ عَنْ الْمَلْعُونِ فِرْعَوْنَ إذْ طَغَى … فَأُغْرِقَ فِي الْيَمِّ انْتِقَامًا بِغَضْبَةِ
وَكُلَّ كَفُورٍ مُشْرِكٍ بِإِلَهِهِ … وَآخَرَ طَاغٍ كَافِرٍ بِنُبُوَّةِ
كَعَادٍ ونمروذ وَقَوْمٍ لِصَالِحِ … وَقَوْمٍ لِنُوحِ ثُمَّ أَصْحَابِ أَيْكَةِ
وَخَاصِمْ لِمُوسَى ثُمَّ سَائِرِ مَنْ أَتَى … مِنْ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ مُحْيِيًا لِلشَّرِيعَةِ
عَلَى كَوْنِهِمْ قَدْ جَاهَدُوا النَّاسَ إذْ بَغَوْا … وَنَالُوا مِنْ الْمَعَاصِي بَلِيغَ الْعُقُوبَةِ
translated_text:
and never be angry with anyone who sheds blood,
Or steals the wealth of someone in need;

Nor one who reviles another’s guarded honour, however exalted,
Nor one who engages in illicit intercourse;

Nor one who bars people’s passage along their roads,
Nor one who spreads corruption throughout the earth;

Nor one who bears false witness, lying and fabricating,
Nor one who accuses chaste women of fornication;

Nor one who deliberately destroys crops and offspring,
Nor one who judges people in return for bribes.

Restrain your tongue from blaming anyone who spreads corruption,
And never punish anyone for a crime.

Ease the way for those who deliberately lie about their Lord—
For everyone who brings forth a fabrication—

Even if they intend to mislead those who heed them,
Seeking to corrupt humankind and then gain leadership.

Plead for the accursed Pharaoh, who transgressed
And was drowned in the sea in wrathful retribution;

And for every hardened disbeliever who associates partners with his God,
And every other tyrant who denies prophethood:

Such as ‘Ād, Nimrod, the people of Sālih,
The people of Noah, and the people of the Thicket.

Argue against Moses, and all the other prophets
Who came to revive the divine law,

For having fought people when they transgressed
And inflicted severe punishment for disobedience.

وَإِلَّا فَكُلُّ الْخَلْقِ فِي كُلِّ لَفْظَةٍ … وَلَحْظَةِ عَيْنٍ أَوْ تَحَرُّكِ شَعْرَةِ
وَبَطْشَةِ كَفٍّ أَوْ تَخَطِّي قَدِيمَةٍ … وَكُلِّ حَرَاكٍ بَلْ وَكُلِّ سَكِينَةِ
همو تَحْتَ أَقْدَارِ الْإِلَهِ وَحُكْمِهِ … كَمَا أَنْتَ فِيمَا قَدْ أَتَيْتَ بِحُجَّةِ
وَهَبْكَ رَفَعْتَ اللَّوْمَ عَنْ كُلِّ فَاعِلٍ … فِعَالَ رَدًى طَرْدًا لهذي الْمَقِيسَةِ
فَهَلْ يُمْكِنُ رَفْعُ الْمَلَامِ جَمِيعِهِ … عَنْ النَّاسِ طَرًّا عِنْدَ كُلِّ قَبِيحَةِ؟
وَتَرْكُ عُقُوبَاتِ الَّذِينَ قَدْ اعْتَدَوْا … وَتَرْكُ الْوَرَى الْإِنْصَافَ بَيْنَ الرَّعِيَّةِ
فَلَا تُضْمَنَنْ نَفْسٌ وَمَالٌ بِمِثْلِهِ … وَلَا يُعْقَبَنْ عَادٌ بِمِثْلِ الْجَرِيمَةِ
وَهَلْ فِي عُقُولِ النَّاسِ أَوْ فِي طِبَاعِهِمْ … قَبُولٌ لِقَوْلِ النَّذْلِ مَا وَجْهُ حِيلَتِي؟
وَيَكْفِيكَ نَقْضًا مَا بِجِسْمِ ابْنِ آدَمَ … صَبِيٍّ وَمَجْنُونٍ وَكُلِّ بَهِيمَةِ
مِنْ الْأَلَمِ الْمَقْضِيِّ فِي غَيْرِ حِيلَةٍ … وَفِيمَا يَشَاءُ اللَّهُ أَكْمَلُ حِكْمَةِ
إذَا كَانَ فِي هَذَا لَهُ حِكْمَةٌ فَمَا … يُظَنُّ بِخَلْقِ الْفِعْلِ ثُمَّ الْعُقُوبَةِ؟
وَكَيْفَ وَمِنْ هَذَا عَذَابٌ مُوَلَّدٌ … عَنْ الْفِعْلِ فِعْلِ الْعَبْدِ عِنْدَ الطَّبِيعَةِ؟
كَآكِلِ سُمٍّ أَوْجَبَ الْمَوْتَ أَكْلُهُ … وَكُلٌّ بِتَقْدِيرِ لِرَبِّ الْبَرِيَّةِ
translated_text:
Otherwise, all creatures, in every word,
Every glance of an eye or movement of a hair,
Every stroke of a hand or step of a foot,
Every motion—indeed, every moment of stillness—
Are subject to Allah’s decrees and His judgment,
Just as you are, according to the argument you have offered.

Suppose you absolve everyone who commits
Ruinous deeds, carrying this analogy through:

Can all blame possibly be lifted
From everyone for every vile deed?

Can punishment of transgressors be abandoned,
And people cease to uphold justice among their subjects,

So that no life or property is compensated with its equivalent,
And no aggressor punished in proportion to his crime?

Would people’s reason or natural disposition accept
The scoundrel’s plea: “What could I do?”

Sufficient to refute you is what afflicts the body of a human being—
A child or an insane person—and every beast:

Pain decreed, with no means of averting it;
And in whatever Allah wills lies perfect wisdom.

If He has wisdom in this, what then should be thought
Of His creating the deed and then imposing punishment?

How could it be otherwise, when some such suffering arises
As a natural consequence of the act—the servant’s own act?

Like someone who eats poison, whose eating causes death:
All of this is decreed by the Lord of creation.

original_text:
فَكُفْرُكَ يَا هَذَا كَسُمِّ أَكَلْتَهُ … وَتَعْذِيبُ نَارٍ مِثْلُ جَرْعَةِ غُصَّةِ
أَلَسْتَ تَرَى فِي هَذِهِ الدَّارِ مَنْ جَنَى … يُعَاقَبُ إمَّا بالقضا أَوْ بِشِرْعَةِ؟
وَلَا عُذْرَ لِلْجَانِي بِتَقْدِيرِ خَالِقٍ … كَذَلِكَ فِي الْأُخْرَى بِلَا مَثْنَوِيَّةِ
وَتَقْدِيرُ رَبِّ الْخَلْقِ لِلذَّنْبِ مُوجِبٌ … لِتَقْدِيرِ عُقْبَى الذَّنْبِ إلَّا بِتَوْبَةِ
وَمَا كَانَ مِنْ جِنْسِ الْمَتَابِ لِرَفْعِهِ … عَوَاقِبَ أَفْعَالِ الْعِبَادِ الْخَبِيثَةِ
كَخَيْرِ بِهِ تُمْحَى الذُّنُوبُ وَدَعْوَةٍ … تُجَابُ مِنْ الْجَانِي وَرَبِّ شَفَاعَةِ
وَقَوْلُ حَلِيفِ الشَّرِّ إنِّي مُقَدَّرٌ … عَلَيَّ كَقَوْلِ الذِّئْبِ هذي طَبِيعَتِي
وَتَقْدِيرُهُ لِلْفِعْلِ يَجْلِبُ نِقْمَةً … كَتَقْدِيرِهِ الْأَشْيَاءَ طَرًّا بِعِلَّةِ
فَهَلْ يَنْفَعَنْ عُذْرُ الْمَلُومِ بِأَنَّهُ … كَذَا طَبْعُهُ أَمْ هَلْ يُقَالُ لِعَثْرَةِ؟
أَمْ الذَّمُّ وَالتَّعْذِيبُ أَوْكَدُ لِلَّذِي … طَبِيعَتُهُ فِعْلُ الشُّرُورِ الشَّنِيعَةِ؟
فَإِنْ كُنْتَ تَرْجُو أَنْ تُجَابَ بِمَا عَسَى … يُنْجِيكَ مِنْ نَارِ الْإِلَهِ الْعَظِيمَةِ
translated_text:
Thus your disbelief, O man, is like poison you have eaten;
The torment of the Fire is like a choking draught.

Do you not see that in this world an offender
Is punished, whether by divine decree or revealed law?

The Creator’s decree affords the offender no excuse;
So too in the Hereafter, without exception.

The Lord of creation’s decreeing a sin entails
His decreeing its consequences—unless repentance intervenes,

Or something akin to repentance in removing
The consequences of His servants’ wicked deeds:

Such as good deeds through which sins are erased, or an answered prayer
Offered by the offender or an intercessor.

The evildoer’s saying, “It was decreed for me,”
Is like the wolf’s saying, “This is my nature.”

His decreeing a deed that brings retribution
Is like His decreeing all things through causes.

Does it help the blameworthy to plead
That such is their nature? Does it win pardon for their lapse?

Or are blame and punishment all the more warranted
For one whose nature is to commit atrocious evils?

So if you hope to receive an answer that might
Save you from Allah’s dreadful Fire,

original_text:
فَدُونَكَ رَبُّ الْخَلْقِ فَاقْصِدْهُ ضَارِعًا … مُرِيدًا لِأَنْ يَهْدِيَكَ نَحْو الْحَقِيقَةِ
وَذَلِّلْ قِيَادَ النَّفْسِ لِلْحَقِّ وَاسْمَعَنْ … وَلَا تُعْرِضَنْ عَنْ فِكْرَةٍ مُسْتَقِيمَةِ
وَمَا بَانَ مِنْ حَقٍّ فَلَا تَتْرُكَنَّهُ … وَلَا تَعْصِ مَنْ يَدْعُو لِأَقْوَمِ شِرْعَةِ
وَدَعْ دِينَ ذَا الْعَادَاتِ لَا تَتْبَعَنَّهُ … وَعُجْ عَنْ سَبِيلِ الْأُمَّةِ الْغَضَبِيَّةِ
وَمَنْ ضَلَّ عَنْ حَقٍّ فَلَا تَقْفُوَنَّهُ … وَزِنْ مَا عَلَيْهِ النَّاسُ بالمعدلية
هُنَالِكَ تَبْدُو طَالِعَاتٌ مِنْ الْهُدَى … تُبَشِّرُ مَنْ قَدْ جَاءَ بِالْحَنِيفِيَّةِ
بِمِلَّةِ إبْرَاهِيمَ ذَاكَ إمَامُنَا … وَدِينِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ خَيْرِ الْبَرِيَّةِ
فَلَا يَقْبَلُ الرَّحْمَنُ دِينًا سِوَى الَّذِي … بِهِ جَاءَتْ الرسل الْكِرَامُ السَّجِيَّةِ
وَقَدْ جَاءَ هَذَا الْحَاشِرُ الْخَاتَمُ الَّذِي … حَوَى كُلَّ خَيْرٍ فِي عُمُومِ الرِّسَالَةِ
وَأَخْبَرَ عَنْ رَبِّ الْعِبَادِ بِأَنَّ مَنْ … غَدَا عَنْهُ فِي الْأُخْرَى بِأَقْبَحِ خَيْبَةِ
فهذي دِلَالَاتُ الْعِبَادِ لِحَائِرِ … وَأَمَّا هُدَاهُ فَهُوَ فِعْلُ الرُّبُوبِيَّةِ
وَفَقْدُ الْهُدَى عِنْدَ الْوَرَى لَا يُفِيدُ مَنْ … غَدَا عَنْهُ بَلْ يَجْرِي بِلَا وَجْهِ حُجَّةِ
translated_text:
Then turn to the Lord of creation in humble supplication,
Seeking that He guide you to the truth.

Make your soul yield its reins to the truth, and listen;
Do not turn away from sound reflection.

Whatever truth becomes clear, never abandon it;
Do not disobey one who calls to the most upright way.

Abandon the religion of those bound by custom; do not follow it,
And turn aside from the path of the people who incurred wrath.

Do not follow anyone who has strayed from the truth;
Weigh people’s beliefs and practices impartially.

Then the first gleams of guidance appear,
Bringing glad tidings to whoever comes with the upright faith—

The creed of Abraham, our leader,
And the religion of Allah’s Messenger, the best of creation.

The Most Merciful accepts no religion except that
Which the messengers of noble character brought.

Now has come this Gatherer, the Seal of the Prophets,
Whose universal message encompasses every good.

He conveyed from the Lord of His servants that whoever
Turns away from him faces the bitterest loss in the Hereafter.

Such is the direction servants can offer the bewildered;
But guiding him belongs to the Lord alone.

Lack of guidance among mankind does not avail
One who turns away from it; he proceeds without a valid plea.

original_text:
وَحُجَّةُ مُحْتَجٍّ بِتَقْدِيرِ رَبِّهِ … تَزِيدُ عَذَابًا كَاحْتِجَاجِ مَرِيضَةِ
وَأَمَّا رِضَانَا بِالْقَضَاءِ فَإِنَّمَا … أُمِرْنَا بِأَنْ نَرْضَى بِمِثْلِ الْمُصِيبَةِ

يَسُوقُ أُولِي التَّعْذِيبِ بِالسَّبَبِ الَّذِي … يُقَدِّرُهُ نَحْوَ الْعَذَابِ بِعِزَّةِ
translated_text:
The plea of one who invokes his Lord’s decree
Only increases his torment, like an ailing woman’s plea.

As for our contentment with the decree,
We are commanded only to accept such things as calamities:

Illness and poverty, humiliation and exile,
And any harm unaccompanied by wrongdoing.

As for deeds that He dislikes us to perform,
We must not approve what He abhors merely because He wills it.

Some scholars have said: “There must be no approval
Of acts of disobedience and major sins.”

Another group says: “We are content with His decreeing,
But not with the thing decreed—that vilest of deeds.”

Others say: “We accept these deeds insofar as they are attributed
To Him, but meet what pertains to us with displeasure.”

For these deeds are the Lord’s creation,
Yet, for His creatures, they are not mere acts of instinct.

Thus we accept them insofar as He creates them,
But abhor them as acts by which sin is incurred.

The accountable servant’s disobedience is his neglect
Of what his Lord commands, even though it occurs by His will.

For the Lord of creation has truly declared
That His servants will be in Hell or Paradise.

Just as they experience the like in this world;
Even beasts experience suffering and ease.

Whatever distinctions His supreme wisdom has ordained,
It has ordained with knowledge, might, and mercy.

In His might, He drives those destined for punishment
Towards torment through the means He decrees;

and He guides those destined for bliss towards their bliss
Through sincere deeds performed in hope and fear.

The command of creation’s God is plainly the means
By which He leads those destined for bliss towards happiness.

For whoever is destined for happiness, His commands take effect
By making righteous deeds easy for him.

But whoever is destined for misery attains no happiness
Through command or prohibition, for misery has been decreed.

The servant cannot escape what has been decreed for him,
Yet he chooses what is good or shameful.

He is not compelled, bereft of will;
Rather, he wills through a will created in him.

Among the most wondrous things is the creation of a will
Through which he comes to choose guidance over error.

Thus your question, “Did he choose to abstain for a wise purpose?”
Is like asking, “Did he choose to cease willing?”

I choose not to choose a deed of error;
Were I to achieve such abstention, I would attain repentance.

This is possible, but it depends
On what Allah wills of the one endowed with will.

translated_text:
Shaykh al-Islām said:

Section

I have mentioned elsewhere that the Qadariyyah are “of three types”: “polytheistic Qadariyyah,” “Magian Qadariyyah,” and “Iblīs-like Qadariyyah.”

The first are those who acknowledge divine decree and predestination and claim that this accords with divine commands and prohibitions. They say:

“Had Allah willed, neither we nor our forefathers would have associated partners with Him, nor would we have forbidden anything”—and so on, in Sūrat al-An‘ām.

“And those who associated partners with Allah said, ‘Had Allah willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him’”—in Sūrat al-Nahl.

And in Sūrat al-Zukhruf:

“And they said, ‘Had the Most Merciful willed, we would not have worshipped them.’”

Their position ultimately leads to nullifying the revealed laws, commands, and prohibitions, while acknowledging Allah’s universal lordship over every creature, and that there is no creature but that my Lord holds it by its forelock. This frequently afflicts groups among the Sufis and the fuqarā (the poor)—whether as a belief or a state—until some of them go so far as to permit forbidden things, dispense with obligations, and abolish

punishments, although they cannot sustain this in practice. They act upon it only when it accords with their desires, as did the Arab polytheists. Then, whenever someone’s desires are opposed, he rises to resist that opposition, transgressing all bounds and observing no limit—just as the polytheists also used to do. This approach becomes self-contradictory when human wills conflict: one person wants something, while another wants its opposite, and both wills are divinely decreed. One must therefore give precedence to one of them, to some alternative, or to each in a particular respect; otherwise, chaos necessarily follows. The adherents of this approach may go to such extremes that they identify existing things themselves with Allah, as has been discussed elsewhere.

They invoke conformity with Allah’s decretive will to justify the evil deeds committed by themselves and others, as in al-Harīrī’s statement:

“I disbelieve in a Lord who is disobeyed.”

Likewise, when one of his companions was invited by a toll collector and was told, “He is a toll collector,” he replied:

“Even if he has disobeyed the command, he has obeyed the will.”

And Ibn Isrā’īl said:

“I am now subject to whatever He chooses for me;
Thus all my deeds are acts of obedience.”

They sometimes call this “reality,” considering it the reality of lordship, the reality that actually exists, or descriptive reality. Since these people have an admixture of Christianity, and Christians have an admixture of polytheism, they followed the polytheists in invoking divine decree in opposition to the revealed law. This is despite their worshipping others besides Allah, who decreed all that exists; these people, too, have an admixture of that.

 فَيَقُولُونَ:
 خَالِقُ الْخَيْرِ، غَيْرُ خَالِقِ الشَّرِّ،
 وَيَقُولُ مَنْ كَانَ مِنْهُمْ فِي مِلَّتِنَا:
 إنَّ الذُّنُوبَ الْوَاقِعَةَ لَيْسَتْ وَاقِعَةً بِمَشِيئَةِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى،
 وَرُبَّمَا قَالُوا:
 وَلَا يَعْلَمُهَا أَيْضًا وَيَقُولُونَ: إنَّ جَمِيعَ أَفْعَالِ الْحَيَوَانِ وَاقِعٌ بِغَيْرِ قُدْرَتِهِ وَلَا صُنْعِهِ فَيَجْحَدُونَ مَشِيئَتَهُ النَّافِذَةَ وَقُدْرَتَهُ الشَّامِلَةَ؛
 وَلِهَذَا قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ:
 الْقَدَرُ نِظَامُ التَّوْحِيدِ فَمَنْ وَحَّدَ اللَّهَ وَآمَنَ بِالْقَدَرِ تَمَّ تَوْحِيدُهُ وَمَنْ وَحَّدَ اللَّهَ وَكَذَّبَ بِالْقَدَرِ نَقَضَ تَكْذِيبُهُ تَوْحِيدَهُ. وَيَزْعُمُونَ أَنَّ هَذَا هُوَ الْعَدْلُ وَيَضُمُّونَ إلَى ذَلِكَ سَلْبَ الصِّفَاتِ، وَيُسَمُّونَهُ التَّوْحِيدَ كَمَا يُسَمِّي الْأَوَّلُونَ التلحيد التَّوْحِيدَ فَيُلْحِدُ كُلٌّ مِنْهُمَا فِي أَسْمَاءِ اللَّهِ وَصِفَاتِهِ وَهَذَا يَقَعُ كَثِيرًا إمَّا اعْتِقَادًا وَإِمَّا
translated_text:
When their heretics, who are their leaders, go further, they say:

“We worship none but Allah, since nothing exists besides Him.”

One of their leaders said, “The Christians disbelieved only because they restricted their worship.” On this basis, they sanction the worship of everything that exists and endorse the polytheists’ worship of idols and stones. Yet they regard the polytheists as falling short because they restricted worship to certain manifestations and individual entities. Clearly, such restriction is common to all polytheists: although they share in polytheism, they differ widely in the gods they worship. One worships the sun, another the moon, another al-Lāt, another al-‘Uzzā, and another Manāt, the third and last. Each takes his own desire as his god and worships whatever appeals to him. The same applies to the worship of human graves: each fixes his devotion on the likeness of someone of whom he thinks well.

The “second group of Qadariyyah” are the Magian type: those who ascribe partners to Allah in His creation, just as the former ascribed partners to Him in His worship. They say:

“The creator of good is different from the creator of evil.”

Those among them who belong to our religious community say:

“The sins that occur do not occur by the will of Allah Most High.”

Sometimes they also say, “Nor does He know of them.” They say that all the acts of living beings occur without His power or His making, thus denying His unfailing will and all-encompassing power. For this reason, Ibn ‘Abbās said:

“Divine decree is the binding thread of belief in Allah’s oneness. Whoever affirms Allah’s oneness and believes in divine decree has perfected his belief in His oneness. Whoever affirms Allah’s oneness but rejects divine decree has that belief undone by his rejection.”

They claim that this is justice, and they combine it with the negation of Allah’s attributes, which they call monotheism—just as the former call heresy monotheism. Thus both groups deviate concerning Allah’s names and attributes. This often occurs either as a belief or

حَالًا فِي كَثِيرٍ مِنْ الْمُتَفَقِّهَةِ وَالْمُتَكَلِّمَةِ. كَمَا وَقَعَ اعْتِقَادُ ذَلِكَ فِي الْمُعْتَزِلَةِ، وَالشِّيعَةِ الْمُتَأَخِّرِينَ وَابْتُلِيَ بِبَعْضِ ذَلِكَ طَوَائِفُ مِنْ الْمُتَقَدِّمِينَ مِنْ الْبَصْرِيِّينَ وَالشَّامِيِّينَ وَقَدْ يُبْتَلَى بِهِ حَالًا لَا اعْتِقَادًا بَعْضُ مَنْ يَغْلِبُ عَلَيْهِ تَعْظِيمُ الْأَمْرِ وَالنَّهْيِ مِنْ غَيْرِ مُلَاحَظَةٍ لِلْقَضَاءِ وَالْقَدَرِ. وَلِمَا بَيْنَ الطَّائِفَتَيْنِ مِنْ التَّنَافِي تَجِدُ الْمُعْتَزِلَةَ أَبْعَدَ النَّاسِ عَنْ الصُّوفِيَّةِ وَيَمِيلُونَ إلَى الْيَهُودِ وَيَنْفِرُونَ عَنْ النَّصَارَى وَيَجْعَلُونَ إثْبَاتَ الصِّفَاتِ هُوَ قَوْلُ النَّصَارَى بِالْأَقَانِيمِ وَلِهَذَا تَجِدُهُمْ يَذُمُّونَ النَّصَارَى أَكْثَرَ كَمَا يَفْعَلُ الْجَاحِظُ وَغَيْرُهُ كَمَا أَنَّ الْأَوَّلِينَ يَمِيلُونَ إلَى النَّصَارَى أَكْثَرَ. وَلِهَذَا كَانَ هَؤُلَاءِ فِي الْحُرُوفِ وَالْكَلَامِ الْمُبْتَدَعِ كَمَا كَانَ الْأَوَّلُونَ فِي الْأَصْوَاتِ وَالْعَمَلِ الْمُبْتَدَعِ كَمَا اقْتَسَمَ ذَلِكَ الْيَهُودُ وَالنَّصَارَى؛ وَالْيَهُودُ غَالِبُهُمْ قَدَرِيَّةٌ بِهَذَا الِاعْتِبَارِ؛ فَإِنَّهُمْ أَصْحَابُ شَرِيعَةٍ وَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ عَنْ الْحَقِيقَةِ الْقَدَرِيَّةِ.
 وَلِهَذَا تَجِدُ أَرْبَابَ الْحُرُوفِ وَالْكَلَامِ الْمُبْتَدَعِ كَالْمُعْتَزِلَةِ يُوجِبُونَ طَرِيقَتَهُمْ وَيُحَرِّمُونَ مَا سِوَاهَا وَيَعْتَقِدُونَ أَنَّ الْعُقُوبَةَ الشَّدِيدَةَ لَاحِقَةٌ مَنْ خَالَفَهَا حَتَّى إنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ:
 بِتَخْلِيدِ فُسَّاقِ أَهْلِ الْمِلَلِ وَيُكَفِّرُونَ مَنْ خَرَجَ عَنْهُمْ مِنْ فِرَقِ الْأُمَّةِ وَهَذَا التَّشْدِيدُ وَالْآصَارُ وَالْأَغْلَالُ شِبْهُ دِينِ الْيَهُودِ. وَتَجِدُ أَرْبَابَ الصَّوْتِ وَالْعَمَلِ الْمُبْتَدَعِ لَا يُوجِبُونَ وَلَا يُحَرِّمُونَ؛ وَإِنَّمَا يَسْتَحِبُّونَ وَيَكْرَهُونَ فَيُعَظِّمُونَ طَرِيقَهُمْ وَيُفَضِّلُونَهُ وَيُرَغِّبُونَ فِيهِ حَتَّى يَرْفَعُوهُ
translated_text:
as a state of mind among many of those engaged in jurisprudence and speculative theology. This became a doctrinal belief among the Muʿtazilah and the later Shīʿah, while some earlier groups in Basra and Syria were afflicted with aspects of it. Some people may also be afflicted with it as a state of mind rather than a belief, when their reverence for divine commands and prohibitions predominates without due regard for divine decree and predestination.

Because these two groups are mutually opposed, you find the Muʿtazilah furthest removed from the Sufis. They incline towards the Jews and recoil from the Christians, equating affirmation of Allah’s attributes with the Christian doctrine of the divine Persons. Hence they are more given to censuring Christians, as al-Jāhiz and others do, whereas the former group inclines more towards Christians. Thus these concern themselves with letters and innovated discourse, just as the former concern themselves with sounds and innovated practices—a division resembling that between Jews and Christians. Most Jews are Qadariyyah in this respect: they adhere to a religious law but turn away from the reality of divine decree.

Thus you find those devoted to letters and innovated discourse, such as the Muʿtazilah, declaring their own way obligatory and every other way forbidden. They believe that severe punishment will befall anyone who opposes it. They even maintain that sinners among the adherents of religious communities will remain in Hell forever, and declare those groups within the Muslim community that depart from their way to be disbelievers. This severity, these burdens and shackles, resemble the religion of the Jews.

By contrast, you find those devoted to sound and innovated practices declaring nothing obligatory or forbidden, but merely recommending or discouraging. They exalt their way, proclaim its superiority, and encourage others to follow it, until they elevate it

original_text:
فَوْقَ قَدْرِهِ بِدَرَجَاتِ. فَطَرِيقُهُمْ رَغْبَةٌ بِلَا رَهْبَةٍ إلَّا قَلِيلًا كَمَا أَنَّ الْأَوَّلَ رَهْبَةٌ فِي الْغَالِبِ بِرَغْبَةِ يَسِيرَةٍ وَهَذَا يُشْبِهُ مَا عَلَيْهِ النَّصَارَى مِنْ الْغُلُوِّ فِي الْعِبَادَاتِ الَّتِي يَفْعَلُونَهَا مَعَ انْحِلَالِهِمْ مِنْ الْإِيجَابِ وَالِاسْتِحْبَابِ لَكِنَّهُمْ يَتَعَبَّدُونَ بِعِبَادَاتِ كَثِيرَةٍ وَيَبْقَوْنَ أَزْمَانًا كَثِيرَةً عَلَى سَبِيلِ الِاسْتِحْبَابِ. وَالْفَلَاسِفَةُ يَغْلِبُ عَلَيْهِمْ هَذَا الطَّرِيقُ كَمَا أَنَّ الْمُتَكَلِّمِينَ يَغْلِبُ عَلَيْهِمْ الطَّرِيقُ الْأَوَّلُ.
وَالْقِسْمُ الثَّالِثُ:
 الْقَدَرِيَّةُ الإبليسية الَّذِينَ صَدَّقُوا بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ صَدَرَ عَنْهُ الْأَمْرَانِ. لَكِنَّ عِنْدَهُمْ هَذَا تَنَاقُضٌ وَهُمْ خُصَمَاءُ اللَّهِ كَمَا جَاءَ فِي الْحَدِيثِ.
 وَهَؤُلَاءِ كَثِيرٌ فِي أَهْلِ الْأَقْوَالِ وَالْأَفْعَالِ مِنْ سُفَهَاءِ الشُّعَرَاءِ وَنَحْوِهِمْ مِنْ الزَّنَادِقَةِ كَقَوْلِ أَبِي الْعَلَاءِ المعري:
أَنَهَيْت عَنْ قَتْلِ النُّفُوسِ تَعَمُّدًا … وَزَعَمْت أَنَّ لَهَا مُعَادًا آتِيًا
مَا كَانَ أَغْنَاهَا عَنْ الْحَالَيْنِ 
(١)
وقول بَعْضِ السُّفَهَاءِ الزَّنَادِقَةِ:
 يَخْلُقُ نُجُومًا وَيَخْلُقُ بَيْنَهَا أَقْمَارًا. يَقُولُ يَا قَوْمُ غُضُّوا عَنْهُمْ الْأَبْصَارَ. تَرْمِي النسوان وَتَزْعَقُ مَعْشَرَ الْحُضَّارَ. اُطْفُوا الْحَرِيقَ وَبِيَدِك قَدْ رَمَيْت النَّارَ. وَنَحْوَ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا يُوجِبُ كُفْرَ صَاحِبِهِ وَقَتْلِهِ.
original_footnote:
(١) سقط بعض قول المعري لخرم في الأصل
قال الشيخ ناصر بن حمد الفهد (ص ٧٤):
وأبيات المعري هي:
صرف الزمان مفرق الإلفين … فاحكم إلهي بين ذاك وبيني
أنهيت عن قتل النفوس تعمدا … وبعثت أنت لقبضها ملكين
وزعمت أن لها معادا ثانيا … ما كان أغناها عن الحالين
translated_text:
far above its proper rank. Their way is thus one of hope with scarcely any fear, whereas the former way is predominantly fear with little hope. This resembles the Christians’ excesses in the acts of worship they practise, despite casting off obligation and recommendation. Nevertheless, they perform many acts of worship and persist in them for long periods as recommended devotions. This way predominates among the philosophers, just as the former way predominates among the speculative theologians.

The third category is the Qadariyyah of Iblīs, who acknowledge that both the command and the decree come from Allah, but regard this as a contradiction. They are Allah’s adversaries, as stated in the hadith.

Such people are numerous among those devoted to discourse and practices: foolish poets and other heretics like them. An example is the saying of Abū al-‘Alā’ al-Ma‘arrī:

“Have You forbidden the deliberate taking of lives … and claimed that a return awaits them?
How little need they had of either state!” (1)

Another is the saying of one of these foolish heretics:

“He creates stars, and among them He creates moons.
He says, ‘O people, lower your eyes before them.’
You send women forth and cry, ‘You who are gathered here,
Put out the blaze!’ Yet Your own hand cast the fire.”

These and similar utterances render their speaker a disbeliever and liable to execution.
translated_footnote:
(1) Part of al-Ma‘arrī’s verse is missing owing to a lacuna in the original. Shaykh Nāsir ibn Hamad al-Fahd states (p. 74):
Al-Ma‘arrī’s verses are:

Time’s vicissitudes part two companions … Judge, my God, between time and me.
Have You forbidden the deliberate taking of lives … yet sent two angels to take them?
You claimed that they would return once more … How well they could have done without either state!

translated_text: Reflect, then, on how the sound faiths—those of the believers, the Jews, the Christians, and the Sabians—originally had no Qadariyyah among them. Rather, the Qadariyyah arose from the two false faiths: those of the Magians and the polytheists. However, the Christians and those who resembled them inclined toward the Sabians, while the Jews and those who resembled them (1)

translated_text:
Shaykh al-Islām, the mufti of mankind and heir to the early generations, Abū al-‘Abbās Ahmad ibn Taymiyyah—may Allah Most High have mercy on him—was asked about people who invoke the prior divine decree as an excuse, saying:

“The matter has already been settled: the wretched are wretched, and the blessed are blessed.” They cite as evidence the words of Allah, glorified be He:

“Indeed, those for whom the best reward from Us has already been decreed will be kept far away from it.”

They maintain that Allah has decreed good and evil, that fornication is decreed for us, and that we have no power over our actions; rather, power belongs to Allah alone. They say that we guard against what has been decreed for us, that Adam did not disobey, and that whoever says, “There is no god but Allah,” will enter Paradise. They cite as evidence the Prophet’s words, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“Whoever says, ‘There is no god but Allah,’ will enter Paradise, even if he commits fornication and even if he steals.”

Please explain to us the falsity of this group’s claims with decisive proofs.

He replied—may Allah Most High have mercy on him:

All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all worlds. If these people persist in this belief, they are greater in disbelief than the Jews and Christians. For the Jews and Christians believe in divine commands and prohibitions, promises and threats, reward and punishment. Yet they have engaged in distortion and alteration, believing in some and rejecting others. As Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers, and wish to make a distinction between Allah and His messengers, saying, ‘We believe in some and disbelieve in others,’ and wish to adopt a way in between—”

“But those who believe in Allah and His messengers and make no distinction between any of them—to them He will grant their rewards. And Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful.”

If someone who believes in some and disbelieves in others is truly a disbeliever, then what of someone who rejects everything and acknowledges neither Allah’s commands and prohibitions nor His promises and threats, but instead disregards all of this, invoking divine decree as an excuse? His disbelief is greater than that of someone who believes in some and disbelieves in others.

The falsity of these people’s claim becomes clear in several ways:

First: Each of them either considers divine decree an excuse for a person or does not. If divine decree is an excuse for a person, then it is an excuse for everyone, since all are equally subject to it. It would therefore follow that he must not condemn anyone who wrongs him, insults him, takes his wealth, corrupts his household, cuts off his head, or destroys crops and livestock. Yet all these people are liars who contradict themselves.

Each of them continually censures one person, hates another, and opposes another. Indeed, they hate, show hostility toward, and condemn the very person who challenges their views. If divine decree were an excuse for someone who commits forbidden acts and neglects obligations, they would have to refrain from censuring or hating anyone, or calling anyone a wrongdoer, no matter what he did.

It is well known that no one can act in this way. If people did so, the world would perish. Thus, their claim is demonstrably unsound according to reason, just as it constitutes disbelief according to the revealed law. They are liars and fabricators when they claim that divine decree is an excuse for a person.

Second: This would imply that Iblīs, Pharaoh, and the people of Noah

and ‘Ād, and everyone whom Allah destroyed for their sins, would be excused. This is disbelief according to the consensus of the adherents of all religions.

(Third): This would imply making no distinction between Allah’s allies and His enemies, between believers and disbelievers, or between the people of Paradise and the people of Hell.

Allah Most High says:

“The blind and the seeing are not equal,

nor are darkness and light,

nor shade and scorching heat,

nor are the living and the dead equal.”

He Most High also says:

“Or should We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like those who spread corruption on earth? Or should We treat those who fear Allah like the wicked?”

And He Most High says:

“Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, alike in their life and their death? How evil is their judgment!”

For Allah had already determined the destinies of all these people and recorded their decrees before creating them. Yet they are divided into those who are blessed through faith and righteous deeds, and those who are wretched through disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience. This establishes that divine decree and predestination provide no one with an excuse for disobeying Allah.

Fourth: We believe in divine decree, but we do not invoke it as an excuse. Whoever invokes divine decree as an excuse has an invalid argument, and whoever pleads divine decree offers an unacceptable excuse. Were such an argument acceptable, it would have been accepted from Iblīs and other sinners. Fifth: The Prophet was asked about this. He said:

“There is not one of you whose place in Paradise and whose place in Hell have not already been written.” He was asked, “O Messenger of Allah, should we not then abandon deeds and rely on what has been written?” He replied, “No. Act, for everyone will be enabled to do that for which he was created.”

Reported by al-Bukhārī and Muslim. In another hadith in al-Sahīh, he was asked:

“O Messenger of Allah, tell us about the deeds people do and strive at: do they concern matters for which the pens have already dried and the scrolls have been rolled up, or matters they undertake anew in light of what has come to them?”—or words to that effect. He replied, “Rather, they concern matters for which the pens have already dried and the scrolls have been rolled up.” He was then asked, “What, then, is the point of deeds?” He replied, “Act, for everyone will be enabled to do that for which he was created.”

Sixth: It may be said that Allah knew all things and recorded them as they truly are. He, glorified be He, recorded that a certain person would believe and do righteous deeds, and thus enter Paradise, while another would disobey and act wickedly, and thus enter Hell. Likewise, He knew and recorded that a certain person would marry a woman and have intercourse with her, and thus have a child; that another would eat and drink, and thus have his hunger and thirst satisfied; and that another would sow seeds, and thus crops would grow.

Whoever says, “If I am destined to be among the people of Paradise, I will enter it without righteous deeds,” makes a false and self-contradictory statement. For Allah knew that he would enter Paradise through his righteous deeds. If he were to enter it without deeds, that would contradict what Allah knew and decreed.

A comparable example is someone who says, “I will not have intercourse with a woman. If Allah has decreed that I should have a child, it will be born.” Such a person is ignorant, for when Allah decrees that a child will be born, He decrees that its father will have intercourse with a woman, who will then conceive and give birth. As for a child without pregnancy or intercourse, Allah has neither decreed nor recorded that.

Likewise, Allah has prepared Paradise only for the believers. Whoever thinks that he will enter Paradise without faith is mistaken. If he believes that the deeds Allah has commanded are unnecessary, and that it makes no difference whether he performs them or not, he is a disbeliever. Allah has forbidden Paradise to the disbelievers. Thus, this belief contradicts the faith whose possessor will not enter the Fire.

Section

As for His words, Most High:

“Indeed, those for whom We have already decreed the finest reward will be kept far away from it.”

Anyone for whom Allah has already decreed the finest reward must become a pious believer. Whoever is not among the believers has not had the finest reward decreed for him by Allah. Rather, when Allah has decreed something beforehand for a servant, He directs him to perform the deeds by which he will attain what was decreed for him. This is like someone for whom Allah has decreed that he will have a child: he must have intercourse with a woman and cause her to conceive. For Allah, glorified be He, has decreed both causes and their effects; both have been decreed by Him beforehand. Whoever thinks that the finest reward has been decreed by Allah for anyone without a cause has gone astray. Rather, He, glorified be He, facilitates both causes and their effects, and He has decreed both beforehand.

Section

As for the statement, “We have no power over any of our actions,” whoever says this has spoken falsely. Allah, glorified be He, has distinguished between those who have power and ability and those who do not. He says:

“So fear Allah as much as you are able.”

And He says:

“And pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by those who are able to undertake it.”

And He, Most High, says:

“Allah is the One who created you in weakness, then gave you strength after weakness, then weakness and grey hair after strength.”

Allah has affirmed that the servant has a will and performs actions. As He, Most High, says:

“For whoever among you wills to take a straight path.”

“But you do not will unless Allah, Lord of the worlds, wills.”

And He says:

“As a reward for what they used to do.”

Yet Allah, glorified be He, is the servant’s Creator and the Creator of all his power, will, and deeds. For there is no Lord besides Him and no god other than Him. He is the Creator, Lord, and Sovereign of all things.

Section

As for the statement, “Unlawful sexual intercourse and other sins have been decreed for us,” this is true, but invoking it as an excuse does the speaker no good. Allah has written down His servants’ deeds, both good and evil, and their eventual misery or bliss. He has made deeds a cause of reward and punishment and has written all of this down, just as He has written down illnesses and made them a cause of death, and has written down the ingestion of poison and made it a cause of illness and death. Whoever consumes poison becomes ill or dies. Allah has decreed and written down both the cause and its consequence. Likewise, whoever commits what he has been forbidden—disbelief, wickedness, or disobedience—does what has been written down for him, yet deserves the recompense Allah has written down for whoever does such things.

These people’s appeal to divine decree to excuse their sins is of the same kind as the argument of the polytheists, about whom Allah said:

“The polytheists said, ‘Had Allah willed, neither we nor our forefathers would have worshipped anything besides Him, nor would we have forbidden anything without His authority.’ Those before them did the same.”

And He, Most High, said:

“The polytheists will say, ‘Had Allah willed, neither we nor our forefathers would have associated partners with Him, nor would we have forbidden anything.’”

Allah, Most High, said:

“Likewise, those before them denied the truth until they tasted Our punishment. Say, ‘Do you have any knowledge that you can produce for us? You follow nothing but conjecture, and you do nothing but guess.’”

“Say, ‘The conclusive argument belongs to Allah. Had He willed, He would have guided you all.’”

Whoever says that Adam did not disobey is denying the Quran and must be called upon to repent; if he does not repent, he is put to death. For Allah said:

“Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray.”

Disobedience means contravening Allah’s revealed command. Whoever contravenes the command with which Allah sent His Messengers and revealed His Books has disobeyed, even though his action falls within what Allah has destined and decreed. These people imagined that disobedience means going beyond Allah’s decree. But this is impossible, for no created being can go beyond Allah’s decree. If disobedience meant only this, then neither Iblīs, Pharaoh, the people of Noah, ʿĀd, Thamūd, nor any of the disbelievers would be disobedient either, because they all fall within Allah’s decree.

The person who says this is then beaten and humiliated. If he complains of being wronged by whoever treated him this way, he is told: “The person who did this is not disobedient, for he falls within Allah’s decree, like all other created beings.” Whoever makes this claim contradicts himself and cannot maintain a consistent position.

As for the claim, “Whoever says, ‘There is no god but Allah,’ will enter Paradise,” and the appeal to the aforementioned hadith, the response is:

There is no doubt that the Quran and Sunnah contain both promises and warnings. Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, those who unjustly consume the property of orphans are only consuming fire into their bellies, and they will burn in a blazing Fire.”

Allah Most High also says:

“O you who believe, do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly, but only through trade by mutual consent. And do not kill yourselves. Indeed, Allah is ever Merciful to you.”

“And whoever does that in aggression and injustice, We will cast him into a Fire. And that is easy for Allah.”

There are many such passages in the Quran and Sunnah. The servant must believe in both, rather than believe in some and disbelieve in others. These polytheists wanted to believe in the promises while denying the warnings. The Harūriyyah and the Muʿtazilah wanted to believe in the warnings but not the promises. Both groups were mistaken.

The position of Ahl al-Sunnah wa-l-Jamāʿah is to believe in both the promises and the warnings. Yet deeds already existed before we did, so there is no point in exhausting oneself with deeds or restraining oneself from pleasures, since what was written in pre-eternity will inevitably occur. translated_text:
‘Everything is Allah’s creation and belongs to Him. He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.’

He said, ‘May Allah have mercy on you. I only asked you this to sharpen your understanding. Two men from Muzayna came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, “O Messenger of Allah, tell us about what people do today and strive to accomplish: is it something already decreed for them and settled by a prior decree, or does it concern what lies ahead of them, in light of what their Prophet has brought them and the proof that has been established against them?”

He replied, “No. Rather, it is something already decreed for them and settled. This is confirmed in the Book of Allah:

‘By the soul and the One who fashioned it, then inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness.’”’”

Muslim also narrated in his Sahīh, from Zuhayr, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir ibn ‘Abd Allah, who said:

“Surāqa ibn Mālik ibn Ju‘shum came and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, explain our religion to us as though we had only just been created. What is the nature of our deeds today? Do they concern matters for which the pens have dried and the decrees have already been issued, or matters yet to be determined?’

He replied, ‘No. Rather, they concern matters for which the pens have dried and the decrees have already been issued.’

He asked, ‘Then what is the point of striving?’

Zuhayr said, ‘Then Abū al-Zubayr said something I did not understand, so I asked what he had said. He replied, “Strive, for everyone is enabled to act.”’”

In another wording:

“The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Everyone who acts is enabled to perform his deeds.’”

In the two Sahīhs, ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib, may Allah be pleased with him, reported:

“We were attending a funeral in Baqī‘ al-Gharqad when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to us. He sat down, and we sat around him. He had a short staff with him. He lowered his head and began poking the ground with his staff. Then he said, ‘There is not one of you—not a single soul brought into existence—whose place in Paradise or the Fire Allah has not already written down, and who has not already been recorded as wretched or blessed.’

A man said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, should we not rely on what has been written for us and give up striving? Whoever is

among the blessed will come to perform the deeds of the blessed, and whoever is among the wretched will come to perform the deeds of the wretched.’

He replied, ‘Strive, for everyone is enabled to act. The blessed will be enabled to perform the deeds of the blessed, and the wretched will be enabled to perform the deeds of the wretched.’ Then he recited:

‘As for the one who gives and fears Allah,
and believes in the best reward,
We will make easy for him the way of ease.
But as for the one who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient,
and denies the best reward,
We will make easy for him the way of hardship.’”

In al-Bukhārī’s version:

“‘Should we not rely on what has been written for us and give up striving? Whoever among us is among the blessed will come to perform the deeds of the blessed, and whoever is among the wretched will come to perform the deeds of the wretched.’ And he said, ‘As for the deeds of the blessed’”—and the hadith continues.

In another version in the two Sahīhs, ‘Alī said:

“One day, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had a stick in his hand with which he was poking the ground. He raised his head and said, ‘There is not a soul among you whose place in Paradise or the Fire is not already known.’

They said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, why, then, should we strive? Should we not rely on this?’

He replied, ‘No. Strive, for everyone is enabled to do that for which he was created.’ Then he recited, ‘As for the one who gives and fears Allah, and believes in the best reward,’ through to His words, ‘We will make easy for him the way of hardship.’”

In these and other hadiths, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, thus conveyed what the Quran also indicates: that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, knew, recorded, and decreed beforehand whether His servants would ultimately be blessed or wretched, just as He knew and recorded beforehand other matters concerning His servants and other beings. The same meaning is also conveyed in Sahīh Muslim in the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn Asīd al-Ghifārī. The scriptural texts and transmitted reports concerning Allah’s prior knowledge, His recording, ordaining, and determining things before their creation are exceedingly numerous and varied.

translated_text:

Their abandonment of the deeds incumbent upon them is itself part of what was decreed, through which they were enabled to perform the deeds of the wretched. For the blessed are those who do what is commanded and refrain from what is forbidden. Whoever abandons the obligatory deeds he has been commanded to perform and does what is forbidden, relying on the decree, is among the wretched who are enabled to perform the deeds of the wretched.

This answer given by the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is entirely sound and correct. It resembles his answer in the hadith reported by al-Tirmidhī:

“He was asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about medicines with which we treat ourselves, healing recitations we ask to have recited over us, and protective measures we take? Do they ward off anything Allah has decreed?’ He replied, ‘They are part of Allah’s decree.’”

This is because Allah—glorified and exalted is He—knows things as they truly are, and likewise records them. If He knows that they will come about through causes, whether human actions or otherwise, and has decreed and determined that they will occur in this way, it is not permissible to suppose that those things will occur without the causes Allah has appointed for them. This applies to all events.

For example, if Allah knows and has recorded that a child will be born to a particular couple, and Allah, glorified is He, has made this dependent upon the parents coming together in intercourse and the emission of the lowly fluid from which the child is conceived, then the child cannot come into existence without the cause upon which its existence was made dependent, even though causes are of “two kinds”: ordinary and extraordinary.

{فَأَنْزَلْنَا بِهِ الْمَاءَ فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ مِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَرَاتِ}
 .
 وَقَالَ:
 
{وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ}
 وَأَمْثَالُ ذَلِكَ. فَجَمِيعُ ذَلِكَ مُقَدَّرٌ مَعْلُومٌ مَقْضِيٌّ مَكْتُوبٌ قَبْلَ تَكْوِينِهِ؛ فَمَنْ ظَنَّ أَنَّ الشَّيْءَ إذَا عُلِمَ وَكُتِبَ أَنَّهُ يَكْفِي ذَلِكَ فِي وُجُودِهِ وَلَا يَحْتَاجُ إلَى مَا بِهِ يَكُونُ مِنْ الْفَاعِلِ الَّذِي يَفْعَلُهُ، وَسَائِرِ الْأَسْبَابِ؛ فَهُوَ جَاهِلٌ ضَالٌّ ضَلَالًا مُبِينًا؛ مِنْ وَجْهَيْنِ. (أَحَدُهُمَا مِنْ جِهَةِ كَوْنِهِ جَعَلَ الْعِلْمَ جَهْلًا؛ فَإِنَّ الْعِلْمَ يُطَابِقُ الْمَعْلُومَ؛ وَيَتَعَلَّقُ بِهِ عَلَى مَا هُوَ عَلَيْهِ؛

 إنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ شَيْئًا بِدُونِ الْأَسْبَابِ؛
 فَقَدْ قَالَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْبَاطِلَ وَهُوَ بِمَنْزِلَةِ مَنْ قَالَ:
 إنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَذَا الْوَلَدَ وُلِدَ بِلَا أَبَوَيْنِ وَأَنَّ هَذَا النَّبَاتَ نَبَتَ بِلَا مَاءٍ فَإِنَّ تَعَلُّقَ الْعِلْمِ بِالْمَاضِي وَالْمُسْتَقْبَلِ سَوَاءٌ فَكَمَا أَنَّ مَنْ أَخْبَرَ عَنْ الْمَاضِي بِعِلْمِ اللَّهِ بِوُقُوعِهِ بِدُونِ الْأَسْبَابِ يَكُونُ مُبْطِلًا؛
 فَكَذَلِكَ مَنْ أَخْبَرَ عَنْ الْمُسْتَقْبَلِ كَقَوْلِ الْقَائِلِ:
 إنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِمَ أَنَّهُ خَلَقَ آدَمَ مِنْ غَيْرِ طِينٍ وَعَلِمَ
translated_text:
the ordinary kind is exemplified by a human being born of two parents, and the extraordinary kind by a human being born of a mother alone, as Jesus was; or of a father alone, as Eve was; or without either parent, as Adam, the father of mankind, was created from clay.

All causes were known to Allah beforehand, recorded by Him, determined and decreed by Him, as were their connections to their effects. The causes through which vegetation is created, such as the sending down of rain and other causes, likewise fall into this category. As the Most High says:

“And the water Allah sends down from the sky, giving life thereby to the earth after its death and dispersing throughout it every kind of creature.”

And He says:

“We sent down water with it and thereby brought forth every kind of fruit.”

And He says:

“We made from water every living thing.”

There are other similar passages. All of this is determined, known, decreed and recorded before it is brought into being. Whoever supposes that something’s being known and recorded suffices for its existence, without its needing that through which it comes into being—the agent who brings it about and all the other causes—is ignorant and manifestly astray in two respects.

The first is that he has turned knowledge into ignorance. Knowledge corresponds to what is known and relates to it as it truly is. Allah, glorified is He, knows that created things come into being through the causes He creates, because that is what actually happens. Whoever claims that He knows something to occur without its causes has spoken falsely about Allah. He is like someone who says that Allah knows that this child was born without parents, or that this vegetation grew without water.

Knowledge relates to the past and the future alike. Just as someone makes a false claim when he speaks of a past event and claims that Allah knows it occurred without its causes, so too does someone who makes such a claim about the future. This is like someone saying: “Allah knew that He created Adam without clay, and knew

that people reproduce without marriage, and that He caused crops to grow without water or soil.” This is false, and its falsehood is apparent to everyone. The same applies to such claims about the future. Likewise, “deeds” are a cause of reward and punishment.

If someone were to say that Allah expelled Adam from Paradise without any sin on his part and decreed this, or that He forgave Adam without repentance and knew this, that would be a lie and a falsehood. By contrast, someone who recites:

“Then Adam received words from his Lord, and He accepted his repentance,”

and:

“They both ate from it, and their nakedness became apparent to them, and they began covering themselves with leaves from Paradise,”

would be speaking the truth. Allah, glorified is He, knew what Adam would do before it occurred, and He knows it after it has occurred.

The same applies to everything He has related in the “accounts of the prophets.” He knew that it was for their sins that He destroyed the peoples of Noah, ʿĀd, Thamūd, Pharaoh, Lot, Midian and others, and that it was for their faith and piety that He saved the prophets and their followers. As He says:

“When they forgot what they had been reminded of, We saved those who forbade evil and seized the wrongdoers with a terrible punishment because of their defiant disobedience.”

And He says:

“Each We seized for his sin: against some We sent a storm of stones; some were overtaken by the mighty blast; some We caused the earth to swallow; and some We drowned,” to the end of the verse.

And He says:

“That is how We repaid them for their transgression.”

And He says:

“So Allah seized them for their sins, and they had no one to protect them from Allah.”

And He says:

“So We destroyed them for their sins and raised up another generation after them.”

And He says:

“There are their houses, lying desolate because of their wrongdoing. Surely in this is a sign for people who know. And We saved those who believed and were mindful of Allah.”

And He says:

“Such is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are doing wrong. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe.”

And He says:

“Thus We established Joseph in the land, to settle wherever he wished. We bestow Our mercy upon whom We will, and We do not let the reward of those who do good go to waste.”

And He says:

“O descendants of those We carried with Noah! Indeed, he was a grateful servant.”

And He says:

“Except the family of Lot, whom We saved before dawn, as a favour from Us. Thus do We reward those who are grateful.”

And He says:

“And your Lord’s gracious promise to the Children of Israel was fulfilled because of their patience.”

There are many similar passages in the Quran.

The same applies to His accounts of the bliss and misery that will result from deeds, as in His words:

“Eat and drink with enjoyment because of what you sent ahead in days gone by.”

And His words, exalted is He:

“That is Paradise, which you have been made to inherit because of what you used to do.”

And His words:

“Those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith—We will unite them with their descendants, without diminishing the reward of their deeds in any way.”

And His words:

“Today I have rewarded them for their patience: they are indeed the triumphant.”

And His words:

“And He rewarded them for their patience with Paradise and silk,” and the verses that follow.

And His words:

“Have the disbelievers been repaid for what they used to do?”

And His words:

“‘What brought you into Saqar?’ They will say, ‘We were not among those who prayed, nor did we feed the poor. We used to indulge in vain talk with those who did so, and we used to deny the Day of Judgement, until death came to us.’ So the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them.”

There are very many similar passages in the Quran. In His accounts of bliss and misery in the Hereafter, He, glorified is He, makes clear that these result from deeds—those commanded and those forbidden—just as He explains the same concerning the punishments and rewards He decrees in this world.

translated_text:
The second point:

Knowing that something will happen, reporting that it will, and recording it do not mean that it can dispense with the causes through which it comes about and without which it cannot occur, such as the agent, his power and his will. Believing that it can is the height of ignorance. Scholars agree that this knowledge does not, in itself, bring the known object into existence. Rather, it corresponds to that object as it actually is, neither imparting an attribute to it nor acquiring an attribute from it.

This is comparable to our knowledge of things that preceded us—things that existed before we came into being—as in our knowledge of Allah, His names and His attributes. Scholars agree that such knowledge has no effect on the existence of its object. Some of our knowledge, however, does affect the existence of its object, such as knowledge that prompts us to act and informs us of an action’s nature and extent. Voluntary actions proceed only from someone possessing awareness and knowledge, since will depends upon the presence of knowledge. This distinction within our knowledge—between active knowledge, which affects its object, and receptive knowledge, which has no effect on its object’s existence—settles the question of knowledge.

Some people say that “knowledge” is a receptive attribute that has no effect on its object, as various groups of speculative theologians maintain. Others say that it is, rather, an active attribute that does affect its object, as various groups of philosophers and speculative theologians maintain. The correct view is that it is of “two kinds,” as we have explained.

The same applies to the knowledge of the Lord—blessed and exalted is He. His knowledge of Himself—glorified is He—has no effect on the existence of its object. His knowledge of His creatures, whom He created by His will and volition, however, does affect the existence of the things He knows. And what is said concerning

speech and recording is the same as what is said concerning knowledge:

When He—glorified and exalted is He—creates something, He creates it through His knowledge, power and will. Creation therefore necessarily implies knowledge and serves as evidence of it, as He, the Exalted, says:

“Does He who created not know, while He is the Subtle, the All-Aware?”

But when He reports what will happen before it happens, His knowledge and report at that point do not bring it into existence, any more than His knowledge and report of it after it exists do. This is so for three reasons:

(First): Knowledge and reports concerning the future are like knowledge and reports concerning the past.

(Second): The knowledge that has an effect is that which entails the will necessarily involved in creation, not that which entails a report. We have already explained the difference between knowledge that directs action and knowledge that conveys information.

(Third): Even if we suppose that knowledge and reports of what will happen have an effect on the existence of what is known and reported, power and will are undoubtedly still necessary. Mere knowledge cannot therefore necessitate its existence without power and will.

It is thus clear that knowledge, reporting and recording do not make it possible to dispense with an agent possessing power and will. Further evidence of this is that Allah—glorified and exalted is He—knows and reports what He Himself will bring about. For example, He knows that He will bring about the Resurrection and reports this. Yet it is well known that this knowledge and report do not necessitate the occurrence of what is known and reported without the causes that Allah has appointed for it.

With this established, the questioner’s statement, “The blessed will not become wretched, and the wretched will not become blessed,”

is correct:

That is, whoever Allah has decreed will be blessed will indeed be blessed, but through the deeds by which He has made him attain blessedness. Likewise, the wretched person becomes wretched only through the deeds by which He has made him become wretched. These include relying on predestination and abandoning obligatory deeds.

As for his statement, “Deeds are not sought for their own sake, but to attain blessedness and avert wretchedness, and deeds already existed before us,” he should be asked: Is it blessedness and wretchedness themselves that have preceded, or their predetermination in knowledge, decree and recording? This is a point of confusion over which many people err, because they do not distinguish between a thing’s being established in knowledge and predetermination and its actual existence and realization. The former consists of knowing it, reporting it and recording it. None of these forms part of the thing itself or of its inherent attributes.

For this reason, many people misunderstand the Prophet’s words—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—in the authentic hadith narrated by Maysara, who said:

“I asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, when were you a prophet?’—or, in another version, ‘When were you recorded as a prophet?’ He replied, ‘When Adam was between soul and body.’”

They therefore suppose that he himself and his prophethood came into existence at that time. This is ignorance, for Allah did not make him a prophet until he was forty years old. He said to him:

“Through Our revelation of this Quran to you, although before it you were among those unaware.”

And He said:

“And He found you lost and guided you.”

In the two Sahīhs it is related:

“When the angel came to him, he said, ‘Read!’ He replied, ‘I cannot read’—three times.”

And whoever says that the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—was a prophet before revelation came to him is a disbeliever by the consensus of the Muslims. Rather, the meaning is that Allah recorded his prophethood, making it known and proclaiming it after creating Adam’s body but before breathing the soul into him. Similarly, the Prophet related that Allah records a child’s provision, lifespan, deeds, wretchedness and blessedness after creating his body but before breathing the soul into him. Thus, in the hadith of al-ʿIrbād ibn Sāriya, narrated by Ahmad and others, the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said:

“I am the servant of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets.”

Another version reads:

“I am the servant of Allah, indeed recorded as the Seal of the Prophets while Adam still lay in his clay. I shall tell you of the earliest signs of this: the supplication of my father Abraham, the glad tidings of Jesus, and my mother’s vision. When she gave birth to me, she saw a light emerge from her that illuminated the palaces of Syria.”

Many ignorant people, including authors and others, narrate it as:

“I was a prophet while Adam was between water and clay,”

or:

“While Adam was neither water nor clay.”

They take this to mean that he himself already existed. Yet Adam was not between water and clay; rather, water is a constituent of clay, not its counterpart.

Since this is so, if he says that what preceded was blessedness and wretchedness themselves, he has spoken falsely. Blessedness can occur only after the blessed person exists; likewise, wretchedness can occur only after the wretched person exists. Similarly, deeds and provision exist only after the doer exists, and provision becomes such only after its recipient exists. What precedes is only the knowledge and predetermination of these things, not the things themselves in their actual existence. Since this is so, deeds also precede in the same sense that blessedness and wretchedness precede. Both are known and decreed, and both

Allah, glorified is He, knew and decreed that one person would do certain deeds and thereby attain blessedness, while another would do certain deeds and thereby become wretched. He knows that righteous deeds bring blessedness, just as He knows all other causes and their effects: He knows that one person will consume poison and die, while another will eat and be satisfied, or drink and have his thirst quenched. Thus, the error in the questioner’s statement becomes clear:

“There is therefore no point in exhausting oneself with deeds or restraining oneself from pleasures, since what was recorded from eternity will inevitably occur.”

What was recorded from eternity is the blessedness of the blessed person through the righteous deeds made easy for him, and the wretchedness of the wretched person through the evil deeds made easy for him. It is not one without the other that was recorded. Whatever the servant is commanded to do that entails exertion or abstention from a desire is among the means by which blessedness is attained.

What has been decreed and recorded is both blessedness and the deeds through which it is attained. If the servant abandons what he has been commanded to do, relying on what has been recorded, that abandonment is itself among the things recorded and decreed through which he becomes wretched. His statement is like that of someone who says:

“I shall neither eat nor drink. If Allah has decreed that my hunger and thirst will be satisfied, that will happen; otherwise, it will not.”

Or someone who says:

“I shall not have intercourse with my wife. If Allah has decreed a child for me, the child will come into being.”

The same applies to someone who mistakenly abandons supplication, or seeking Allah’s help and placing his trust in Him, supposing that such abandonment is one of the spiritual stations of the elect because he focuses on divine decree. All such people are ignorant and astray.

This is supported by what Muslim narrated in his Sahīh from the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—who said:

from Allah, and do not give way to inaction. If something befalls you, do not say, ‘Had I done this, such and such would have happened.’ Rather, say, ‘Allah decreed it, and He does whatever He wills,’ for ‘if’ opens the way for Satan’s work.”

He thus commanded him to strive for what benefits him and to seek Allah’s help, and forbade him from remaining inactive through reliance on divine decree. He then instructed him, when something befalls him, not to despair over what he has missed, but to consider divine decree and surrender the matter to Allah, since at that point he can do nothing else. As one wise man said: “Matters are of two kinds: those about which something can be done, and those about which nothing can be done. One should not remain inactive concerning the former, nor become distressed over the latter.”

In Sunan Abī Dāwūd, it is related:

“Two men brought a dispute before the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—and he ruled against one of them. The man against whom he ruled said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.’ The Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said, ‘Allah censures inaction. Rather, you must act resourcefully. Then, if something overcomes you, say, “Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.”’”

Another hadith states:

“The discerning person is one who holds himself to account and works for what comes after death. The ineffectual person is one who lets his soul follow its desires and indulges in wishful thinking about Allah.”

It was narrated by Ibn Mājah and al-Tirmidhī, who graded it as good.

Shaddād ibn Aws reported that the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said:

“The discerning person is one who holds himself to account and works for what comes after death. The ineffectual person is one who lets his soul follow its desires and indulges in wishful thinking about Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

Some people misread the word as al-fājir (the wicked), whereas the correct reading is al-ʿājiz (the ineffectual)

 إنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا كَانَ وَمَا يَكُونُ وَمَا لَا يَكُونُ لَوْ كَانَ كَيْفَ كَانَ يَكُونُ فَإِنَّ هَذَا مِنْ بَابِ الْعِلْمِ وَالْخَبَرِ بِمَا لَا يَكُونُ لَوْ كَانَ كَيْفَ يَكُونُ كَقَوْلِهِ: 
{لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَا آلِهَةٌ إلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَا}
 وَقَوْلِهِ: 
{وَلَوْ رُدُّوا لَعَادُوا لِمَا نُهُوا عَنْهُ}
 وَقَوْلِهِ: 
{لَوْ خَرَجُوا فِيكُمْ مَا زَادُوكُمْ إلَّا خَبَالًا}
 وَقَوْلِهِ 
{وَلَوْ عَلِمَ اللَّهُ فِيهِمْ خَيْرًا لَأَسْمَعَهُمْ}
 وَأَمْثَالِ ذَلِكَ كَمَا رُوِيَ أَنَّهُ يُقَالُ لِلْعَبْدِ فِي قَبْرِهِ حِينَ يُفْتَحُ لَهُ بَابٌ إلَى الْجَنَّةِ وَإِلَى النَّارِ.
 وَيُقَالُ:
 هَذَا مَنْزِلُك وَلَوْ عَمِلْت كَذَا وَكَذَا أَبْدَلَك اللَّهُ بِهِ مَنْزِلًا آخَرَ. وَكَذَلِكَ يُقَالُ هَذَا لَوْ لَمْ يَقْتُلْهُ هَذَا لَمْ يَمُتْ بَلْ كَانَ يَعِيشُ إلَّا أَنْ يُقَدَّرَ لَهُ سَبَبٌ آخَرُ يَمُوتُ بِهِ وَاللَّازِمُ فِي هَذِهِ الْجُمْلَةِ خِلَافُ الْوَاقِعِ الْمَعْلُومِ وَالْمَقْدُورِ وَالتَّقْدِيرُ لِلْمُمْتَنِعِ قَدْ يَلْزَمُهُ حُكْمٌ مُمْتَنِعٌ وَلَا مَحْذُورَ فِي ذَلِكَ.
translated_text:
in contrast to the discerning, as in the other hadith:

“Everything is by divine decree, even inaction and discernment.”

Here a question occurs to many people: if what is written must inevitably come to pass, would what was written have changed had the servant not performed the deed? This question also arises concerning someone who is killed: had he not been killed, would he have died? Similar questions may also be asked.

The answer is: had this person not performed righteous deeds, he would not have been blessed; and had he not performed evil deeds, he would not have been wretched. This is like saying that Allah knows what has happened, what will happen, and how things that will not happen would have happened if they had occurred. This concerns knowing and describing how something that will not happen would be if it did happen, as in His words:

“Had there been in the heavens and the earth gods besides Allah, both would have fallen into ruin.”

And His words:

“If they were sent back, they would return to what they were forbidden.”

And His words:

“Had they gone out with you, they would only have added to your confusion.”

And His words:

“Had Allah known any good in them, He would have made them hear.”

There are other examples of this, such as the report that, when a door to Paradise and a door to Hell are opened for a servant in his grave, he is told: “This is your dwelling. Had you done such and such, Allah would have given you another dwelling in its place.”

Likewise, one may say of someone: had that man not killed him, he would not have died, but would have continued living, unless another cause had been decreed through which he would die. The implication of this statement runs contrary to the reality that is known and decreed. Supposing an impossibility may entail an impossible consequence, and there is nothing objectionable in that.

translated_text:
A similar case is the report:

“The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out on the day of Badr and told his Companions where the polytheists would fall, saying: ‘This is where so-and-so will fall, and this is where so-and-so will fall.’ Then he entered the shelter and began supplicating earnestly, saying: ‘O Allah, fulfil for me what You have promised me.’”

His knowledge that he would be victorious did not preclude his taking the means by which victory would be granted to him: seeking Allah’s help.

Some people have erred here, supposing that a supplication whose fulfilment is already known—such as the supplication at the end of Surah al-Baqarah—is prescribed solely as an act of worship. This resembles the claim made by some that supplication is nothing more than an act of worship, because what has been decreed will happen whether one supplicates or not.

Such a person should be told: If Allah has made supplication a means of attaining the desired outcome that He has decreed, how can it come about without supplication? This is akin to their saying: “Should we not abandon deeds and rely on what has been written?”

What further clarifies this is that Allah already knows and has written that He will create His creatures, provide for them, cause them to die, and bring them to life. Can it then be thought that this prior knowledge and writing make these things independent of His creating them, His power, and His will? The same applies to Allah’s knowledge of the deeds His servants will perform and of their becoming blessed or wretched through them, just as He knows, for example, that a man will become ill or die through ingesting poison, wounding himself, or the like.

" جُمْهُورُ الْقَدَرِيَّةِ "
 فَهُمْ يُقِرُّونَ بِالْعِلْمِ وَالْكِتَابِ الْمُتَقَدِّمِ لَكِنْ يُنْكِرُونَ
translated_text:
What we have explained is the position of the early generations of this community, its imams, and the majority of the “groups” among the scholars of jurisprudence, hadith, Sufism, speculative theology, and others. Only the extremists among the Qadariyyah disputed this, supposing that prior knowledge precludes commands and prohibitions. They divided into two groups:

One group affirmed commands and prohibitions, reward and punishment, but denied any prior decree, predestination, or written record concerning them. They emerged towards the end of the Companions’ era. When the Companions heard of their innovations, they disavowed them, as did Abd Allāh ibn Umar, Abd Allāh ibn Abbās, Jābir ibn Abd Allāh, Wāthilah ibn al-Asqaʿ, and others, who also refuted them. The “imams,” including Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and Ahmad, explicitly declared the disbelief of those who deny Allah’s eternal knowledge.

The second group acknowledges Allah’s prior knowledge and written record, but claims that these dispense with commands, prohibitions, and deeds, and that there is no need to act. Rather, whoever has been decreed to be blessed will enter Paradise without any deeds whatsoever, while whoever has been decreed to be wretched will become wretched without any deeds. These people do not constitute a recognized sect among the doctrinal schools; rather, this is something many ignorant people say. They are greater in disbelief and further astray than the former group. Their position amounts to nullifying commands and prohibitions, the lawful and unlawful, and the promise of reward and threat of punishment. They are far greater in disbelief than the Jews and Christians. These are the people whose position the questioner asked about.

As for the “majority of the Qadariyyah,” they acknowledge prior knowledge and the written record, but they deny

translated_text:
that Allah created people’s deeds and that He wills all that occurs. Opposing them are the Qadariyyah who uphold compulsion, who say that the servant has no real power or will and is not truly an agent. All these are misguided innovators.

Worse still are those who regard Allah’s creation of deeds and His willing all that occurs as precluding commands and prohibitions, like the polytheists who said:

“Had Allah willed, neither we nor our forefathers would have associated partners with Him, nor would we have forbidden anything.”

These people are greater in disbelief than the Jews and Christians. Their position amounts to nullifying all the commands and prohibitions brought by all the messengers.

Furthermore, their position is contradictory and self-evidently false. Human life cannot be sustained on this basis, since it necessarily entails humanity’s ruin. If people were subject to no commands or prohibitions, everyone would be free to do whatever he desired. As Allah Most High says:

“Had the Truth followed their desires, the heavens and the earth would have been ruined.”

Thus, if it were said that everyone should be allowed to do whatever he desires—killing people, committing indecencies, taking wealth, and so forth—this would be the utmost corruption. For this reason, no human society can survive without some form of law containing commands and prohibitions, even if instituted by a king and flawed in other respects.

If it is said:

“What you have explained shows that Allah’s prior knowledge and written record concerning blessedness, wretchedness, and other matters do not preclude these things from depending on the deeds and causes through which

This is something people have disputed, just as they have disputed whether ability must accompany the act or must precede it. Among the proponents of affirmation, those who say that ability exists only alongside the act maintain that the servant cannot do anything other than what he actually does, which was already encompassed by Allah’s knowledge and written record.

Those who say that ability may precede the act and may exist without it maintain that the servant can do what he has not done, including what Allah knew and recorded that he would not do.

The decisive answer is that “ability” occurs in Allah’s Book in two senses. The first is the ability required for an act, upon which commands and prohibitions depend, as in His words, Most High:

“Pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by people who are able to make their way to it.”

And His words:

“So fear Allah as much as you are able.”

And His words:

“If any of you cannot afford to marry free believing women”—to the end of the verse.

“Whoever cannot find one must fast for two consecutive months before the two touch one another; and whoever is unable must feed sixty needy people.”

And His words:

“And those who are able to fast must pay a ransom by feeding a needy person.”

And the Prophet’s words, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to ‘Imrān ibn al-Azāriqah:

“Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; and if you cannot, then lying on your side.”

The ability denied here—whether its absence is being reported or brought about—is not the ability upon which commands and prohibitions depend. If that ability were absent, commands and prohibitions, promises and threats, praise and blame, reward and punishment would likewise cease to apply. It may, however, be said that the ability here is like the ability denied in al-Khidr’s words to Moses:

Thus, it is understood to be opposed to the impediments within a person that prevent his heart from willing and performing the act.
